_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: A VM's Terminal tab attaches to its web terminal sessions, until the VM's view closes. Workspace mode and the VM tabs are on; the screen is the default 393x727 phone. exe.dev is faked: the VM "web" is running, its settings fail to load, and it lists the web terminal sessions "ios-1" and "coral" (closing one ends it). The fake terminal server answers each session's "init" message with the output "$ ". Calls: "open" returns the sessions with a terminal connection open now, as a JSON list sorted alphabetically except that the session the page created (once there is one) comes last; "first message" returns the type, session and whether cols is over 20 of the first message any session got, as JSON ("none" before one); "inits" returns the sessions that got an "init" message, in order, as a JSON list; "coral got ls" and "coral got pwd" say whether the input data the page sent session coral, joined, contains "ls" (resp. "pwd"), "true" or "false"; "new session" returns "ok" once a session other than ios-1 and coral has connected, and makes {{MINTED}} its name; "relist" makes the fake list the sessions ios-1, coral and {{MINTED}}; "closed" returns the sessions the page has ended, as a JSON list. Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does. "The tabs" are the buttons inside the navigation element named "VM tabs"; "the session tabs" are the elements with data-testid "vm-terminal-session"; "the terminals" are the elements with data-testid "vm-terminal". Keys are typed key by key into the focused element. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /vm/web/page. There should be exactly 3 tabs, and the last should have data-testid exactly "view-tab-terminal". Unopened, there is no shell: there are no terminals (count 0). 2. Click data-testid "view-tab-terminal": the URL path should become exactly /vm/web/terminal, and the element with data-testid "vm-terminal" should be visible. 3. The session tabs' texts should be exactly "ios-1", "coral", in that order, and the last should have aria-selected="true" (the newest is attached). 4. Call "first message" until it returns {"cols_over_20":true,"session":"coral","type":"init"}. 5. Type "ls"; call "coral got ls" until it returns "true". 6. Picking another session attaches to it too, showing only it: click the first session tab. Call "open" until it returns ["coral","ios-1"]. There should be exactly 2 terminals, and exactly 1 of them visible. 7. Switching back reuses the first connection: click the second session tab, type "pwd", and call "coral got pwd" until it returns "true". Call "inits": it must return ["coral","ios-1"]. 8. A new session gets a color name, as the web terminal's do: click data-testid "vm-terminal-new". There should be exactly 3 session tabs, and the last one's trimmed text must match /^[a-z]+$/. Call "new session" until it returns "ok"; the last session tab's trimmed text must be exactly "{{MINTED}}". Call "open" until it returns ["coral","ios-1","{{MINTED}}"]. 9. Another tab keeps the sessions attached; leaving the VM detaches them: click data-testid "view-tab-page". No terminal should be visible (visible count 0), and call "open" must return ["coral","ios-1","{{MINTED}}"]. Navigate to /: call "open" until it returns []. 10. Coming back attaches to the session last attached, while it lasts: call "relist", then navigate to /vm/web/terminal. The last session tab should have aria-selected="true", and call "open" should return ["{{MINTED}}"]. 11. Closing it ends it and attaches to the newest left: click the last element with data-testid "vm-terminal-close". The session tabs' texts should be exactly "ios-1", "coral"; call "closed" must return ["{{MINTED}}"]; call "open" should return ["coral"].

steps.expression: (() => { const tabs = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="vm-terminal-session"]'); const text = tabs[tabs.length-1]?.textContent?.trim() ?? ''; return /^[a-z]+$/.test(text) ? 'match' : 'no:' + text; })()
